title: A one-page day-trip plan with your pet
excerpt: Map four checkpoints and one simple backup step for a short outing with your pet.
body:
## Four checkpoints
Short outings can change. A single page makes the next step easy to see. This is a day plan, not a moving guide or a long packing list.

## 1. Leave
Write down where and roughly when you will set off. Check the address and route before leaving.

## 2. Arrive
Note the first stop and who needs to know you arrived, if anyone.

## 3. Midday
Note where you can pause and offer your pet water. An approximate time is enough.

## 4. Return
Write down when you expect to head home and the simplest shorter version of the outing if plans shift.

## One line for essentials
List only what this outing calls for: water and a bowl, your pet’s usual essentials, and an appropriate lead or carrier. Check any venue or transport conditions directly with the operator; this guide does not certify their rules.

## When the day changes
Choose one backup step: shorten the trip, move the return time or call your named contact. Keep addresses and phone numbers in a private copy, not a public Story. If bringing your pet no longer makes sense that day, change the plan.

## Copy the page
Leave — time/place ___, pet need ___, backup ___; arrive — ___; midday — water/pause ___; return — ___; contact — private copy only ___.

## Useful sources
- RSPCA — pet travel guidance (rspca.org.uk)
- AVMA — travel preparation brochure (avma.org)
